nodes.summary: Let $L_n$ be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$. This proposition asserts that the sequence $\mathbb{E}[L_n]/n$ converges to a real number as $n \to \infty$. Chvátal and Sankoff proved that it holds.

This is the proposition $0.792665992 \le C$.

nodes.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, a finite sequence of bits $z$ is a common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ if $z$ is obtained both from $x$ and from $y$ by deleting some (possibly no) entries and keeping the remaining entries in order.
nodes.title: Common subsequence

nodes.summary: Write $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ for the length of a longest common subsequence of binary strings $x$ and $y$ of equal length. Let $x_1, y_1$ be binary strings of length $m$ and $x_2, y_2$ binary strings of length $n$, and write $x_1x_2$ and $y_1y_2$ for the concatenated strings of length $m + n$. Then $\mathrm{LCS}(x_1, y_1) + \mathrm{LCS}(x_2, y_2) \le \mathrm{LCS}(x_1x_2, y_1y_2)$.
nodes.title: Superadditivity of the LCS length under concatenation

nodes.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, the length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ of a longest common subsequence equals the largest $k \le n$ such that $x$ and $y$ have a common subsequence of length $k$ (such $k$ exist, since the empty sequence is a common subsequence).
nodes.title: The LCS length as a bounded maximum

nodes.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, let $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ be the length returned by the dynamic-programming algorithm for the longest common subsequence on $x$ and $y$. Then some common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ has length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$, and every common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ has length at most $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$.
nodes.title: The LCS length is the maximum common-subsequence length

nodes.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, the length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ of a longest common subsequence satisfies $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y) \le n$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
